OpenMC-Fusion-Benchmarks (commit 653d6aba04d993d2915a4e4e983e2a2119fa0e27), benchmark.py `_build_source`: the angle bins [0, 360] degrees go through np.cos before the unit conversion, then the cosines are multiplied by pi/180 and used as the limits of the polar cosine distribution. Running OFB's own function on its specification gives mu uniform on [-0.00495, 0.01745] about the reference direction (0, 1, 0), not [-1, 1]: the source is emitted in a thin ring perpendicular to y, not isotropically. The function also returns the last source object, not the list. FARIS does not use this code path; its runner builds an isotropic point source.

Same function: the specification's `weights` are the probabilities of the energy intervals (they equal the MCNP sp1 entries of the IAEA input exactly) but are passed to openmc.stats.Tabular as histogram densities, which OpenMC weights by the interval width. Run on the specification, the mean source energy is 14.637 MeV instead of 14.031 MeV with the weights read as probabilities, and the 13.57 to 15.00 MeV interval carries 63.1 % instead of 62.0 %. FARIS converts probability to density (divides by the interval width).

specifications.yaml tallies the DAGMC surface 'values: [7]' for both spectra and OFB's post-processing divides by that surface's area. Surface 7 is the id of the outer r = 100 cm sphere in the CSG model; in the DAGMC conversion of oktavian_a.step with OFB's own meshing call (cad_to_dagmc 0.14.3, imprint, the specification's mesh sizes) surface 7 is a 3543 cm2 patch of the r = 19.95 cm sphere (6 is the r = 100 cm sphere), so the tally would see about 70 % of the leakage surface and normalise it by the patch area. The stored experiment is the IAEA table divided by 4 pi (19.5 cm)^2 = 4778.36 cm2, a radius that is neither the sample's outer radius (19.95 cm) nor the shell radius (19.75 cm). Unconfirmed against an OFB end-to-end run, which needs pydagmc (not installed here); see docs/defects/OFB-001.

oktavian_al.step in the OFB-LFS repository (a different file from the oktavian_a.step the specification names) holds five solids with the volumes of full nested spheres (0.0045, 0.0312 and 0.0332 m3 for the shells), not of shells: overlapping solids. The specification does not use it.
